items.title: SD-WAN UX 1.0 to UX 2.0 Migration Lab
items.text:
This lab walks through moving Catalyst SD-WAN devices from UX 1.0 configuration (device templates and centralized policy) to UX 2.0 configuration (configuration groups, policy groups and topology policies).

There are many ways to migrate from UX 1.0 to UX 2.0. This lab explores one of them, a one-by-one (site-by-site) migration. Each organization should evaluate the options and choose the approach that fits it best.

items.title: Lab topology
items.text:
The lab network has one data center and three branches, connected over two transports: INET and MPLS. Every SD-WAN edge router has one link to each transport.

Site Routers System IPs Site ID (UX 1.0) LAN LAN routing Data Center dc-edge1, dc-edge2 10.0.0.11, 10.0.0.12 10 192.168.10.0/30 (dc-edge1), 192.168.10.4/30 (dc-edge2) BGP to dc-core Branch 1 br1-edge 10.0.0.21 21 192.168.21.0/24 OSPF to br1-core Branch 2 br2-edge 10.0.0.22 22 192.168.22.0/24 OSPF to br2-core Branch 3 br3-edge 10.0.0.23 23 192.168.23.0/24 OSPF to br3-core

Addresses for testing

To test reachability across the overlay (for example with ping or traceroute from the core routers in CML), use these addresses:

Router Test address dc-core 192.168.10.10 (Loopback) br1-core 192.168.21.2 br2-core 192.168.22.2 br3-core 192.168.23.2

The control components (SD-WAN Manager, Validator and two Controllers) are at site 100 and reach the transports through the VPN0 and Gateway routers.

items.title: Hub-and-spoke
items.text:
The overlay runs in a hub-and-spoke topology:

  • The DC routers are the hubs. The centralized control policy only lets branches learn TLOCs and routes from the DC site.
  • The branches are the spokes. They build data-plane tunnels only to the DC, not to each other, so branch-to-branch traffic goes through the DC.

This policy is the main thing to keep working during the migration. Steps 3 and 4 make sure branches keep reaching the DC whether a site is still on UX 1.0 or already on UX 2.0.

items.title: What you will do
items.text:
Time: 60 minutes

Steps 1 to 5 are the core lab. Steps 6 and 7 are optional if you have time left.

Step Task 0 Understand how UX 1.0 configuration is converted to UX 2.0 Reading only 1 Verify the current network state Core 2 Define the network (site) hierarchy Core 3 Update the UX 1.0 centralized policy to support the new site IDs Core 4 Define the UX 2.0 topology policy Core 5 Migrate the DC routers from UX 1.0 to UX 2.0 Core 6 Migrate the branch routers from UX 1.0 to UX 2.0 Optional 7 Clean up UX 1.0 configuration Optional

items.title: Lab access
items.text:
1. Open the lab link shared by your proctor to get a pod assigned.

  2. In dCloud, click Jumphost, then under Remote Access click Web RDP.

  3. On the jumphost, open Chrome and use the bookmarks to open SD-WAN Manager and CML.

Credentials

Your proctor shares the credentials for the jumphost, SD-WAN Manager and CML separately.

Tip

Click any screenshot in this guide to zoom in.

items.title: Step 0: Configuration Conversion
items.text:
Before a device can move to UX 2.0, its configuration has to exist in UX 2.0 form. Configuration conversion means translating UX 1.0 objects (device templates, feature templates and policies) into their UX 2.0 equivalents.

This step is already done for you

Conversion can take a lot of time in a real network, and it is a separate topic from migrating devices. To keep this lab focused on the migration (moving routers from UX 1.0 to UX 2.0 safely, one site at a time), the lab starts with the configuration already converted. There is nothing to configure in this step. Read it for background, then continue to Step 1.

items.title: How UX 1.0 maps to UX 2.0
items.text: UX 1.0 UX 2.0 Device template Configuration group Feature templates Features inside feature profiles (System, Transport & Management, Service, CLI Add-on) Device-specific variables (template CSV) Variables filled in when the configuration group is deployed Localized policy (QoS, application visibility) and centralized data policy Policy group (for example with an Application Priority & SLA policy) Centralized control policy (for example hub-and-spoke) Topology policy Site lists (ranges of site IDs) Network hierarchy (sites and groups)

items.title: What is already converted in this lab
items.text:
UX 1.0 object UX 2.0 object already in SD-WAN Manager Device template dc Configuration group dc (profiles system, transport, bgp_lan, cli) Device template branch Configuration group branches (profiles system, transport, ospf_lan, cli) QoS, application visibility and data policy Policy group policy_group with Application Priority policy app_priority

You will build the remaining pieces yourself, because they are central to the migration: the network hierarchy in Step 2 and the topology policy in Step 4.

items.title: Approaches to conversion
items.text:
Organizations usually take one of two approaches:

  • Lean option

    Use the Cisco-provided configuration conversion tool, which converts UX 1.0 to UX 2.0 one-to-one. Fast, and the result closely matches what is running today, including any legacy configuration. Learn more about the tool.

  • Power option

    Build the UX 2.0 configuration from scratch. This takes more effort, but it is a chance to remove legacy configuration that is no longer needed and to reduce the number of configuration groups and policy groups.

Mix and match

You can also combine the options: convert all configuration automatically first, then optimize it before assigning it to devices.

items.title: Step 1: Verify Current Network State
items.text:
Before changing anything, confirm the network is healthy and record how the current UX 1.0 policy identifies sites.

  • Go to Monitor → Devices and verify that all devices have full control and data connections.

  • Go to Configuration → Devices → WAN Edges and confirm that all routers are In Sync and managed by device templates.

  • Go to Configuration → Classic → Policies and verify that the centralized policy is activated.

  • On the same screen, click … next to the policy, then click Preview. Note the site lists the policy uses:

    Site list Site IDs dc 10 branches 20-99

items.title: Why the network hierarchy matters
items.text:
In UX 1.0, centralized policies identify sites through site lists, which are ranges of site IDs typed by hand (for example branches = 20-99). In UX 2.0, SD-WAN Manager uses the network hierarchy instead: a tree of groups and sites below Global, where each site has a name, a site ID and a location.

UX 2.0 features such as topology policies refer to sites and groups in the hierarchy instead of to raw site ID ranges. A well-designed hierarchy means that:

  • policies stay readable, for example "apply hub-and-spoke to group branches",
  • a new site gets the right policy simply by being placed in the right group,
  • devices are deployed to a named site rather than to a bare number.

Why new site IDs?

In this lab, every migrated site gets a new site ID (DC 10 → 110, branches 2x → 12x). The existing UX 1.0 policy matches the old IDs and the new UX 2.0 topology matches the new sites, so a router moves from one policy to the other simply by changing its site ID. This lets you migrate one site at a time while both policies run side by side.

SD-WAN Manager has already created sites such as SITE_10 and SITE_21 automatically from the site IDs of existing devices.

items.title: Tasks
items.text:
• Go to Configuration → Network Hierarchy. Click … next to Global and select Add Site.

  • Create a site with these values, then click Add:

    Name Site ID Address dc 110 Oslo

  • Click … next to Global again and select Add Node.

  • Create a new Group named branches.

  • Click … next to group branches and select Add Site.

  • Create a site with these values, then click Add:

    Name Site ID Address Bergen 121 Bergen

  • Follow the same steps to add two more sites to group branches:

    Name Site ID Address Tromso 122 Tromsø Trondheim 123 Trondheim

    The hierarchy should now look like this:

items.title: Step 3: Update the UX 1.0 Centralized Policy for the New Site IDs
items.text: During migration, some sites run on UX 1.0 and some on UX 2.0. Before moving any router, make sure the UX 1.0 centralized policy keeps working for branches that are still on UX 1.0 after the DC gets its new site ID.

items.title: The current policy
items.text:
The active centralized policy centralized_policy has two parts:

  • Control policy branches-hub-and-spoke, which builds the hub-and-spoke topology.
  • Data policy traffic-data, which sets the forwarding class from the DSCP value (46 → voice, 34 → business, 8 → scavenger).

The control policy uses the two site lists you noted in Step 1: dc (site ID 10) and branches (site IDs 20-99).

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 400}}}%%
flowchart LR
    D["DC<br/>site ID 10"]
    C(["Controllers"])
    P["control policy<br/>branches-hub-and-spoke<br/>accept: site-list dc<br/>reject: everything else"]
    B["Branches<br/>site IDs 20-99"]
    D -- "TLOCs and routes" --> C
    C -- "out, to site-list branches" --> P
    P -- "only DC TLOCs and routes" --> B

In CLI form, the policy that the Controllers run looks like this:

policy
 control-policy branches-hub-and-spoke
  sequence 1
   match tloc
    site-list dc            ! (2) match: which TLOCs are accepted
   action accept
  sequence 11
   match route
    site-list dc            ! (2) match: which routes are accepted
   action accept
  default-action reject
 lists
  site-list branches
   site-id 20-99
  site-list dc
   site-id 10
apply-policy
 site-list branches         ! (1) apply: which routers get the filtered view
  control-policy branches-hub-and-spoke out

items.title: Two different site lists
items.text:
The same policy uses site lists in two places, and they mean different things:

(1) Site list in apply-policy (2) Site list in a match entry Question it answers Who receives the policy? What is accepted? In this policy branches (20-99) dc (10) Effect The Controllers filter what they advertise out to routers at sites 20-99. Only TLOCs and routes that originate at site 10 pass. Everything else hits default-action reject.

The result: each branch only learns TLOCs and routes from the DC, so it builds tunnels only to the DC and sends branch-to-branch traffic through the DC. Routers that are not in the apply list (the DC itself) are not filtered and learn everything.

items.title: What breaks during migration
items.text:
In Step 5 the DC routers move to the new site ID 110. If the policy is left as it is:

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 400}}}%%
flowchart LR
    D2["DC on UX 2.0<br/>site ID 110"]
    P["branches-hub-and-spoke<br/>match site-list dc (10)"]
    B["Branches still on UX 1.0<br/>site IDs 21-23"]
    D2 -- "TLOCs and routes" --> P
    P -- "✗ rejected: 110 is not in site-list dc" --> B

The branches would lose every TLOC and route from the DC, because 110 doesn't match site list dc. Branch traffic to the DC would stop.

items.title: The target policy
items.text:
Add a new match site list, ux2-dc (110), so the policy accepts the DC at both its old and its new site ID. The apply list stays branches, so the policy still only applies to branches that are on UX 1.0.

control-policy branches-hub-and-spoke
 sequence 1
  match tloc
   site-list dc
  action accept
 sequence 11
  match tloc
   site-list ux2-dc
  action accept
 sequence 21
  match route
   site-list dc
  action accept
 sequence 31
  match route
   site-list ux2-dc
  action accept
 default-action reject

Green lines are added in this step. Sequence numbers are assigned by SD-WAN Manager and may differ in your CLI preview.

You also create site list ux2-branches (120-199) for the new branch site IDs. You don't use it in this step. It's ready for later, for example if the UX 1.0 policy needs to reference migrated branches.

Why not just change site list dc to 110?

During the migration both DC site IDs are in use: not every DC router moves at the same moment, and you may need to roll back. Accepting both 10 and 110 keeps branches connected to the DC at every point of the migration.

items.title: Tasks
items.text:
• Go to Configuration → Classic → Policies. In the top right corner, click Custom Options and select Centralized Policy → Lists.

  • Under Site, click New Site List and create two site lists:

    Name Site IDs ux2-dc 110 ux2-branches 120-199

  • In the top right corner, click Custom Options and select Centralized Policy → Topology. Click … next to the policy name and select Edit.

  • In the TLOC sequence, click Sequence Rule and add a rule that matches site list ux2-dc with action Accept. Click Save Match and Actions.

  • On the left, switch from TLOC to Route. Click Sequence Rule and add a rule that matches site list ux2-dc with action Accept. Click Save Match and Actions.

  • Click Save Control Policy. In the pop-up window, click Activate.

  • Click Next and preview the CLI to see the differences. Then click Configure Devices and wait until the policy update succeeds.

items.title: Step 4: Define the UX 2.0 Topology Policy
items.text: In this step you build the same hub-and-spoke policy as in UX 1.0, this time as a UX 2.0 topology policy. The logic doesn't change: branches only learn TLOCs and routes from the DC, and everything else is rejected. What changes is which sites it applies to: the new branch site IDs (121-123) instead of the old ones (20-99).

items.title: UX 1.0 policy vs UX 2.0 topology
items.text:
UX 1.0 branches-hub-and-spoke UX 2.0 branches-hub-and-spoke-v2 Where it's configured Centralized policy (Classic) Configuration → Topology Applies to (who) apply-policy site-list branches (site IDs 20-99) Outbound sites: hierarchy group branches (Bergen 121, Tromso 122, Trondheim 123) Accepts (what) match site-list dc (10) and, after Step 3, ux2-dc (110) Match sites: SITE_10 (10) and dc (110) Default action Reject Reject

The two policies cover different branches and never overlap:

  • A branch that is still on UX 1.0 (site ID 21-23) is in site list branches, so it gets the UX 1.0 policy.
  • A branch that has been migrated (site ID 121-123) is in hierarchy group branches, so it gets the UX 2.0 topology policy.

Moving a branch from one policy to the other only takes a change of its site ID, which happens when it is deployed with the configuration group in Step 6.

Why do the two policies use different site IDs?

  • A site can't be covered by both policies at the same time. If the UX 1.0 policy and the UX 2.0 topology both applied to the same site ID, the Controllers would have two conflicting policies for that site.
  • The UX 1.0 policy can't simply be deactivated first. That would leave the network without any hub-and-spoke policy until the UX 2.0 topology is activated, so branches would learn routes from each other during that gap.

Giving migrated sites new site IDs avoids both problems. Each site is covered by exactly one policy at all times, and sites move to UX 2.0 one at a time.

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 400}}}%%
flowchart LR
    DC["DC<br/>site ID 10 (UX 1.0) or 110 (UX 2.0)"]
    C(["Controllers"])
    P1["UX 1.0 policy<br/>accept: dc, ux2-dc"]
    P2["UX 2.0 topology<br/>accept: SITE_10, dc"]
    B1["Branches on UX 1.0<br/>site IDs 21-23"]
    B2["Branches on UX 2.0<br/>site IDs 121-123"]
    DC -- "TLOCs and routes" --> C
    C --> P1 -- "only DC" --> B1
    C --> P2 -- "only DC" --> B2

Why match both DC sites?

Like the updated UX 1.0 policy, the topology accepts the DC at both its old site ID (SITE_10) and its new one (dc, 110). That way it works no matter whether the DC routers have already been migrated or not, and it stays correct if the DC has to be rolled back.

items.title: Tasks
items.text:
• Go to Configuration → Topology and click Create Topology.

  • Enter a topology name and click Create.

  • Under Add Topology, select Custom.

  • Enter the name branches-hub-and-spoke-v2. Under Outbound Sites, click Add Sites, select group branches and click Save.

  • Click Add Rules. In the first rule, change Type to TLOC, match sites dc and SITE_10, and set the action to Accept. Click Save Match and Actions.

  • Click Add Rules again. In this rule, set Type to Route, match sites dc and SITE_10, and set the action to Accept. Click Save Match and Actions.

  • Confirm the policy looks like the screenshot below, then click Save.

  • Click Close in the bottom right corner. Then click … next to the policy name and select Activate.

  • Preview the CLI to see the differences. Click Deploy, then View Deployment Status, and wait until the policy update succeeds.

No effect yet

No routers are at sites Bergen, Tromso or Trondheim yet, so this policy has no effect on traffic until the branches are migrated in Step 6.

items.title: Step 5: Migrate the DC from UX 1.0 to UX 2.0
items.text:
All the preparation so far leads to this moment:

  • the UX 2.0 configuration groups and policy group are ready (Step 0),
  • the new sites exist in the network hierarchy (Step 2),
  • the UX 1.0 policy accepts the DC at its new site ID (Step 3),
  • the UX 2.0 topology is active for the new branch sites (Step 4).

Now you can start moving sites to UX 2.0. You don't have to move everything at once: pick a few sites to start with, migrate them, check that they work, and then continue with the rest. In this lab you start with the DC, then move the branches in Step 6.

Migrating a site takes three steps:

  1. Detach its routers from the UX 1.0 device template.
  2. Deploy them with the UX 2.0 configuration group, using the new site ID. For the DC, that's configuration group dc and site ID 110.
  3. Deploy the policy group policy_group to them.

Expected: a brief control and data connection flap

Changing a router's site ID resets its control connections and data plane tunnels. When each router gets its new site ID, you'll see a short drop of its control and data connections. This is expected, and the connections come back up on their own.

Rolling back

If you hit a problem with a migrated site, rolling it back is simple: attach its routers back to the old UX 1.0 device template, using the CSV you exported, and set the site ID back to the old value. The UX 1.0 policy still covers the old site IDs, so the site returns to its previous state.

items.title: Detach from the device template
items.text:
• Go to Configuration → Templates. Click … next to the DC device template and select Export CSV. Keep this file: it is useful if you need to roll back. Then click … again and select Detach Devices.

  • Select both DC routers, move them to the right and click Detach.

  • Wait until the detachment succeeds.

Detaching doesn't change the router's configuration

Detaching a device template does not modify the routers' configuration. The routers keep running exactly the same configuration as before, so traffic isn't affected. They are just no longer managed by a device template. The configuration changes only when you deploy the configuration group in the next section.

items.title: Deploy the configuration group
items.text:
• Go to Configuration → Configuration Groups. Expand the dc group and, next to Associated, click Add.

  • Select Manual association and click Add Devices.

  • Select both DC routers and click Save.

  • Click Deploy for the dc configuration group.

  • Fill in the variables for dc-edge1. Set Site Id to the new site ID 110.

    System IP Host Name Site Id vpn1_gi3_ip vpn1_gi3_mask vpn1_bgp_neighbor_ip 10.0.0.11 dc-edge1 110 192.168.10.1 /30 192.168.10.2

  • Select the dc-edge2 router from the Chassis Number list at the top.

  • Fill in the variables for dc-edge2. Set Site Id to the new site ID 110. Click Next.

    System IP Host Name Site Id vpn1_gi3_ip vpn1_gi3_mask vpn1_bgp_neighbor_ip 10.0.0.12 dc-edge2 110 192.168.10.5 /30 192.168.10.6

  • Click Preview CLI to compare the UX 1.0 configuration currently on the router with the new UX 2.0 configuration.

    Expected differences

    The QoS configuration is removed, because no policy group is assigned to the router yet. The router also loses its data policy until the policy group is assigned. Both come back in the next section.

  • After reviewing the configuration, click Deploy. On the next screen, click View Deployment Status and wait until the configuration group is deployed.

items.title: Deploy the policy group
items.text:
• Go to Configuration → Policy Groups. Expand policy_group and, next to Associated, click Add.

  • Click Next, select both DC routers and click Next.

  • Click Associate Devices.

  • In the pop-up window, click Provision Devices.

  • Select both DC routers and click Next.

  • Click Next, then Preview CLI. Verify that the QoS and application visibility settings are added back to the configuration.

  • Click Deploy, then View Deployment Status, and wait until the policy group is deployed.

items.title: Step 6: Migrate the Branches from UX 1.0 to UX 2.0 (Optional)
items.text:
Optional step

This step is optional. Do it if you have time left after Step 5.

Repeat the process from Step 5 for the three branch routers (br1-edge, br2-edge, br3-edge):

  • Export CSV from the branch device template (Configuration → Templates), for rollback.
  • Detach the branch routers from the branch device template.
  • Associate and deploy the branches configuration group (Configuration → Configuration Groups), using the variables below.
  • Associate and deploy policy_group (Configuration → Policy Groups).

Once a branch gets its new site ID (121-123), it is part of the branches hierarchy group and receives the UX 2.0 topology policy branches-hub-and-spoke-v2 from Step 4.

items.title: Variables
items.text:
Use these values when deploying the configuration group. Keep the other pre-filled values (System IP, Host Name) as they are.

Router Site Id vpn1_gi3_ip vpn1_gi3_mask br1-edge 121 192.168.21.1 /24 br2-edge 122 192.168.22.1 /24 br3-edge 123 192.168.23.1 /24

Check your work

Go to Monitor → Devices and confirm that all routers again have full control and data connections, now with the new site IDs.

items.title: Step 7: Cleanup (Optional)
items.text:
Optional step

This step is optional. Do it if you have time left after Step 5.

Do this cleanup only after all sites have been moved to configuration groups and policy groups with the new site IDs, and the network has been running stable for a few weeks. Until then, keep the UX 1.0 configuration in place so that you can still roll back a site if needed.

Once you're confident, remove what is no longer used:

  • Deactivate the old UX 1.0 centralized policy in Configuration → Classic → Policies.
  • Remove the UX 1.0 configuration from SD-WAN Manager: device templates, feature templates, centralized policy and policy lists.
  • Go to Configuration → Topology and edit branches-hub-and-spoke-v2. In both rules (TLOC and Route), remove SITE_10 from the matched sites so that only dc remains. Save the policy and deploy it again.
  • Go to Configuration → Network Hierarchy and remove the old sites that are no longer used: SITE_10, SITE_21, SITE_22 and SITE_23.

Tip

Keep the CSV files you exported from the device templates until you are confident no rollback is needed.

Congratulations, you have completed the lab!
